easy.def: A bird that swims and quacks.
examples: The duck swims.
Ducks quack.
A duck has webbed feet.

more.def: A water bird with a flat beak, webbed feet and a quack.
examples: The duck paddled across the pond.
Baby ducks follow their mother.
A duck dipped its head under the water.
Duck under the branch.
He ducked his head.
She ducked under the rope.

more.def: To bend or move down quickly to get out of the way.
examples: She ducked under the low branch.
He ducked when the ball flew by.
We ducked under the table.

easy.def: A friendly word for a boy or man.
examples: Hey, dude!
That dude is tall.
My cousin is a cool dude.

more.def: A casual word for a man or boy, often used to talk to a friend.
examples: Hey dude, wait for me!
That dude on the skateboard is really good.
Some people call their friends dude.

easy.def: Expected or needed by a time.
examples: The paper is due Friday.
The bus is due at three.
My book is due.

more.def: Expected or needing to be done by a certain time.
examples: My library book is due on Friday.
The train is due at four o'clock.
The report is due next week.

easy.def: A man with a very high rank in some countries.
examples: The duke lived in a castle.
The king spoke to the duke.
A duke is a kind of lord.

more.def: A man of very high rank, just below a prince or a king.
examples: The duke lived in a huge castle on a hill.
In the story, the duke gave a grand party for the whole town.
A duke often owned a lot of land long ago.
The knife is dull.
The scissors are dull.
My pencil is dull.

more.def: Not sharp, or not shiny or interesting.
examples: The knife was too dull to cut the bread.
The old penny was dull and brown.
The long talk was dull.
That was a dumb mistake.
It was a dumb joke.
I felt dumb when I forgot my name.

more.def: Showing poor thinking; silly. It can hurt when used to name-call someone.
examples: Leaving the gate open was a dumb mistake.
He made a dumb joke that no one laughed at.
She felt dumb when she forgot her lines.
The store has a dummy in the window.
The dummy wears a hat.
The dummy is made of plastic.

more.def: A model of a person's body, used to show clothes or to practice on.
examples: The shop window had a dummy wearing a winter coat.
Doctors practiced on a dummy.
A dummy stood in the corner of the tailor's shop.

easy.def: To drop or pour out a lot of something.
examples: Dump the sand out.
He dumped the toys on the floor.
The truck dumped the dirt.

more.def: To drop or pour out a heap of something.
examples: The truck dumped a pile of gravel on the road.
She dumped the puzzle pieces onto the table.
Do not dump trash in the river.

easy.def: A place where trash is taken.
examples: We took the trash to the dump.
The dump is outside town.
The truck drove to the dump.

more.def: A place where garbage is taken and left.
examples: The garbage truck drove to the dump.
Seagulls fly over the town dump.
We took the old couch to the dump.

easy.def: At some time while something goes on.
examples: We talk during lunch.
It rained during the night.
Do not talk during the movie.

more.def: Throughout the time that something goes on, or at some point in it.
examples: The bears sleep during the winter.
It rained several times during the night.
Please stay quiet during the show.

easy.def: Tiny bits of dry dirt in the air or on things.
examples: Dust is on the shelf.
The wind blew dust.
I sneezed from the dust.

more.def: Very small bits of dry dirt or other stuff that collect on things or float in the air.
examples: A thick layer of dust covered the old books.
The truck kicked up a cloud of dust on the dirt road.
A sunbeam showed the dust floating in the air.

easy.def: To wipe the tiny bits of dirt off things.
examples: I dust the table.
She dusted the shelf.
Please dust your room.

more.def: To clean a shelf or table by wiping off the fine powder that settles on it.
examples: He dusted the bookshelves every Saturday.
Mom asked me to dust the furniture.
I dusted the piano with a soft cloth.
It is my duty to feed the fish.
Her duty is to hand out papers.
Setting the table is my duty.

more.def: Something that you must do because it is your job or the right thing to do.
examples: It is a lifeguard's duty to watch the swimmers.
Feeding the dog is my duty each morning.
Voting is a duty of every adult citizen.
